assumptions.summary: All users follow the same single-step strategy so each tread receives comparable events.
Environmental erosion is treated as uniform across surfaces of the same material.
Repairs are limited to full replacement or filling with the same material.
Horizontal and local contact-force variation are neglected in the baseline.
Ascent and descent produce distinct longitudinal placements.
Joint wear is approximated by a product of X and Y marginals.
Each of 1000 time steps contains one or two upward walkers with probabilities Po and 1-Po.
A single weathering rate represents each selected region.

task_reconstruction.decision_boundary: The pipeline yields structured archaeological hypotheses. weaknesses.summary: Equation 3.5 gives an integral over hardness without explicit limits, differential, or a clear definition of the accumulated quantity.
The WVM summary writes G as a population-weight sum while Equation 3.7 separately multiplies by gravity; the interface notation is inconsistent.
Equation 3.12 prints normal-parameter order as sigma then mu and does not make its mixture-index scope as clear as Equation 3.11.
The Gauss Mixtual pseudocode omits initialization, learning rate, explicit loss update, covariance constraints, and a reproducible Y stopping rule.
The algorithm fixes k=2 for Y while the Edinburgh X result has three components; the candidate-count and label logic is not closed.
Table 6 assigns down to the 0.08 m mean and up to the 0.15 m mean, while the surrounding prose reverses those labels.
Equation 4.1 is labelled a consistency or KL-like score but is not normalized, uses a free matrix factor, and lacks zero handling.
Equation 4.2 prints an average-age expression with an inequality but does not show the averaging operator or all step weights.
The six-step, five-accepted example is summarized as above-95-percent reliability even though the displayed interval begins at 0.359.
Equation 4.8 inserts average wear depth and area into Brinell geometry; the square-root radicand is generally invalid and gravity is treated as force.
Equation 4.9 is not a normalized or symmetric KL divergence and has no zero-value convention.
The repair decision is contradictory: RSA below 0.95 is defined as repaired, while the worked example reports a tiny score and concludes no repair.
Equation 4.10 exponentiates the distribution score into repair time without a derivation or uncertainty propagation.
Equation 4.12 compares a percent expression with the numeric threshold 0.05, mixing percentage and fraction units.
Substituting sigma_x=12.1 into Equation 4.14 gives about 2.5826, not the stated 1.14; treating 12.1 as a variance still does not recover 1.14.
The sensitivity baseline p approximately 0.01 per year is outside the stated test range whose upper value is 0.005.
Figure 10 is captioned as different-material wear even though it is the typical-day Po scenario, and the text calls Table 8 Figure 8.
Small labels, watermarks, QR overlays, and the nearly empty page-23 text layer reduce figure legibility and searchability; these are presentation warnings, not author-language evidence.
